title: Southbank Software — SaaS vendor playbook (provider side)
provenance: Draft, 14 October 2026, for the two-sided benchmark (decision 148). The provider's positions on the same 19 topics as the customer-side playbook (northwind-saas), for reviewing a customer's markup of our standard terms. Our standard terms are the Common Paper Cloud Service Agreement v2.1 with the Key Terms used in this suite, so a clean copy deviates from nothing under this playbook either; the two playbooks differ in which direction of change is a departure and how far we will go. Each rule's `source` records the Common Paper rationale or market figure it rests on (see ../common-paper-notes.md) and where our position diverges from the published default. Fictional company; not legal advice; not lawyer validated; written before any two-sided run and not tuned to results. Version 2, 15 October 2026 (BENCHMARK-V2.md P1, decision E-52): eight annex rules V-20 to V-27 added for the DPA and SLA of the bundle, mirroring C-20 to C-27 from the provider's position and grounded in the Common Paper DPA v1.1 and SLA v2.0 pages; the clean bundle (v2/base-csa.json) meets each preferred position. Not frozen until the ambiguity read (P2) and calibration (P8). The 14 October vendor runs used version 1 (19 rules). Version 3 (17 October 2026): V-11, V-15 and V-22 amended after the P8 clean-copy calibration (tough-eval/v2/LAYER-A-FIXES.md), so the clean copy meets them as this provenance states.

rules.title: General liability cap
rules.guidance: Our general cap is mutual and set at the Fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim. Customers ask for more; we can go to 2x on larger deals. Above that, or any uncapped general liability, is escalated.
rules.preferred: Mutual general cap of 1x the Fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.
rules.acceptable: Mutual general cap of up to 2x the 12-month Fees, or a fixed amount up to twice the annual Fees.
rules.escalation: Any general cap above 2x the 12-month Fees, a cap on our liability only, or a cap measured over more than 12 months. Escalate to the Commercial Director.
rules.hardLine: Uncapped general liability, or a cap that applies to the Customer's liability only.
rules.source: CSA default: multiple of fees, 1x; 96% of signed CSAs at 1x and 0.5x caps falling to 2.5% (2026 report). Our acceptable 2x is a concession above the published norm.

rules.title: Increased cap for data, security and confidentiality breaches
rules.guidance: Our standard terms carry an increased cap for breaches of the privacy and security section and of confidentiality. Customers ask for higher multiples; we hold at 3x and resist adding categories.
rules.preferred: Increased Claims limited to breach of the privacy and security section and breach of confidentiality, with an Increased Cap Amount of 2x the 12-month Fees.
rules.acceptable: Increased Cap Amount of up to 3x the 12-month Fees for the same categories.
rules.escalation: Increased Cap Amount above 3x, or any additional category of Increased Claims (for example breach of warranty or of the SLA).
rules.hardLine: Uncapped liability for data or security breaches.
rules.source: CSA default Increased Claims are Sections 3 and 10; only 13% of CSAs include Increased Claims and the 2x supercap is the fastest-growing multiple (0.3% → 2.7%). The customer playbook asks for at least 3x; the two overlap at 3x.

rules.title: Uncapped indemnities and damages-waiver exceptions
rules.guidance: Each party's indemnity is uncapped, mutually, and the damages waiver still applies to it. We accept the modern carve-out for gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud. We do not accept uncapped liability for confidentiality or data breaches, which the increased cap already covers.
rules.preferred: Each Indemnifying Party's indemnification obligation is an Unlimited Claim; the damages waiver excludes Increased Claims and breach of confidentiality.
rules.acceptable: Unlimited Claims extended, mutually, to gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud.
rules.escalation: Unlimited Claims extended to breach of confidentiality, data or security breaches, or any one-sided extension.
rules.hardLine: Uncapped liability on us for anything the Customer's own liability is capped for.
rules.source: CSA default; about 1% of CSAs include Unlimited Claims on the annotated page, rising to 10.2% in the 2026 report with gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud as the examples, which is why that carve-out is acceptable.

rules.title: IP indemnity we give
rules.guidance: We indemnify for IP infringement by the service, with the standard exclusions and the standard remedies ending in a prorated refund. Customers may ask to approve settlements; we accept that. We do not widen the indemnity to their own content, their specifications, or combinations we did not supply.
rules.preferred: IP infringement indemnity with exclusions for unauthorised modification, misuse, combination with items not provided by us, and use of an old version; remedy options ending in a prorated refund; indemnity as the exclusive remedy for such claims.
rules.acceptable: No settlement admitting fault on the Customer's behalf or imposing obligations on the Customer without its consent, not unreasonably withheld.
rules.escalation: Removal of any of the four exclusions, an indemnity for infringement caused by the Customer's specifications, or removal of the exclusive-remedy wording.
rules.hardLine: Indemnity covering Customer Content or third-party products.
rules.source: CSA default (76% keep it); 'sole and exclusive remedy' described as very common; first-party claims excluded by design.

rules.title: Use of Customer Content
rules.guidance: We use Customer Content only to provide, maintain and support the service; the Customer keeps its rights. We need the operational uses (hosting, subprocessors, support access) to run the product.
rules.preferred: Use of Customer Content limited to providing and maintaining the Product and related offerings; Customer retains all rights; Feedback excluded from Customer Content.
rules.acceptable: Use limited to providing and supporting the Product for the Customer, with an express list of operational purposes.
rules.escalation: Restrictions that prevent normal operation (no subprocessors, no support access, no backups), or a licence back to us of the Customer's IP beyond what the service needs.
rules.hardLine: Assignment to the Customer of our IP in the Product or in improvements.
rules.source: CSA default; Feedback deliberately licensed rather than assigned because 'many customers bristle at seeing an assignment'.

rules.title: Machine learning on usage data and content
rules.guidance: Our standard terms permit training on aggregated, de-identified data. A growing share of customers strike it; we accept a prohibition on training on Customer Content provided usage-data analytics survive.
rules.preferred: Usage Data and Customer Content may be used for machine learning after aggregation and de-identification; personal-data obligations unaffected.
rules.acceptable: No training on Customer Content; Usage Data may still be used, aggregated and de-identified, to maintain and improve the Product.
rules.escalation: Prohibition on any analysis of Usage Data, or a prohibition that reaches third-party components we rely on.
rules.source: CSA default clause 'to permit basic training of AI and machine learning models'; prohibitions on AI training rose from under 1% to 14% of signed CSAs (2026 report), so the acceptable tier follows the market.

rules.title: Usage data and feedback
rules.guidance: We use Usage Data to maintain and improve the Product and disclose it only in aggregated, non-identifying form. Feedback is ours to use without an assignment.
rules.preferred: Use of Usage Data to maintain and improve; disclosure only when aggregated and non-identifying; a perpetual licence to use Feedback.
rules.acceptable: Disclosure of aggregated Usage Data limited to named purposes (benchmarks, product statistics).
rules.escalation: No collection or use of Usage Data, or Customer ownership of Feedback.
rules.source: CSA default.

rules.title: Confidentiality
rules.guidance: Mutual obligations with reasonable care, the standard exclusions, and advance notice of compelled disclosure where lawful. Our non-public product information, pricing and roadmap are our Confidential Information.
rules.preferred: Mutual non-use and non-disclosure with at least reasonable care; standard exclusions; compelled disclosure with advance notice where lawful; survival after termination.
rules.acceptable: A longer or indefinite survival period for trade secrets; a stricter standard of care applied mutually.
rules.escalation: Obligations that bind us only, or removal of any standard exclusion.
rules.hardLine: Our pricing, roadmap or non-public product information excluded from Confidential Information.
rules.source: CSA default; confidentiality breaches are Increased Claims by default (see V-02).

rules.title: Suspension of service
rules.guidance: We must be able to suspend for an undisputed balance more than 30 days overdue, for breach of the Restrictions, and for use that materially harms the Product or others, without being obliged to give notice first in an emergency. We reinstate once the issue is resolved.
rules.preferred: Suspension on the three standard grounds, with or without notice, with reinstatement on resolution.
rules.acceptable: Prior notice before suspension except where delay would harm the Product or others; a 10-day grace period for overdue balances.
rules.escalation: Removal of suspension for non-payment, a notice period before suspending for security harm, or a requirement to suspend only the affected Users.
rules.hardLine: No right to suspend for use that materially harms the Product or others.
rules.source: CSA default; the Committee's view that suspension is 'a fairly reasonable risk allocation because it is not permanent termination'. The customer playbook requires an attempt at notice; the two overlap at 'notice except in emergencies'.

rules.title: Payment terms
rules.guidance: Payment within 30 days of invoice, disputes raised in good faith before the due date, undisputed amounts paid on time. We can accept 45 days. We do not add late-payment interest.
rules.preferred: Payment within 30 days of receipt of invoice; good-faith disputes notified before the due date.
rules.acceptable: Payment within 45 days; disputes within 30 days of invoice for automatic payments.
rules.escalation: Payment terms of 60 days or more, payment contingent on acceptance testing, or a right to withhold disputed amounts without notice.
rules.hardLine: Payment terms of 90 days or more.
rules.source: 30 days from receipt in 62% of CSAs; no late fees by design because disputes 'were more often an oversight'. Our 45-day acceptable tier is a concession.

rules.title: Renewal and price increases
rules.guidance: Subscriptions auto-renew with 30 days' notice of non-renewal, and fees may rise by up to 7% on renewal with notice. We can hold increases to 5% and give 60 days' notice.
rules.preferred: Auto-renewal with 30 days' non-renewal notice; fee increases of up to 7% per renewal, on notice before the renewal date.
rules.acceptable: Non-renewal notice of up to 60 days; increases capped at 5% per renewal, or at CPI if higher (a flat 5% cap is acceptable).
rules.escalation: No auto-renewal, no increase permitted for more than one renewal, or a cap below 5%; non-renewal notice above 60 days.
rules.source: 87% of CSAs auto-renew, about 70% with a 30-day window; 29% allow increases on renewal, 'typically 5–8%'; automatic increases fell to 13% of signed CSAs. The customer playbook prefers a 5% cap; the two overlap at 5%. Amended 17 October 2026 (P8 clean-copy calibration, pass 1; tough-eval/v2/LAYER-A-FIXES.md): the escalation trigger 'a cap below CPI' made the clean copy's 5% cap, which this source says both playbooks share, an escalation whenever CPI is above 5% (flagged on p19 by Opus and DeepSeek); it now reads 'a cap below 5%'.

rules.title: Termination and refunds
rules.guidance: Termination for material breach uncured 30 days after notice, and for insolvency, both ways. No termination for convenience mid-term; fees are non-refundable except on the listed triggers.
rules.preferred: Mutual termination for uncured material breach (30 days) and insolvency; no termination for convenience; prorated refunds only on the listed triggers.
rules.acceptable: A customer right not to renew at any time; a cure period of up to 45 days; termination for convenience at the end of the current year of a multi-year term.
rules.escalation: Termination for convenience mid-term, refunds of prepaid fees beyond the listed triggers, or termination rights available to the Customer only.
rules.hardLine: Refund of fees for periods already provided.
rules.source: CSA default; termination for convenience 'uncommon in SaaS subscription agreements', requested by customers wary of unproven products.

rules.title: Return and deletion of data on exit
rules.guidance: We delete Customer Content within 60 days of request, backups and legally required copies excepted; we can do 30 days on request. We cannot purge rotating backups early or certify destruction of them.
rules.preferred: Deletion within 60 days of the Customer's request; return or destruction of Confidential Information; backup and legally required copies retained and protected.
rules.acceptable: Deletion within 30 days; an export window of up to 30 days before deletion; written confirmation of deletion on request.
rules.escalation: Immediate deletion, deletion of backups outside the normal rotation, or certified destruction of backup media.
rules.source: CSA default (60 days, backup and legal retention excepted); no published rationale for the period.

rules.title: Our warranty
rules.guidance: We warrant that we will not materially reduce the Product's general functionality during the subscription, with restore-or-terminate as the exclusive remedy. We do not give fitness, performance or error-free warranties; those belong in the SLA.
rules.preferred: Functionality warranty; notice within 45 days of discovery; 45 days to restore; termination with prorated refund as the exclusive remedy; all other warranties disclaimed.
rules.acceptable: 30 days to restore; a non-infringement warranty limited to known claims.
rules.escalation: Warranties of fitness for purpose, performance against the Customer's requirements, or compliance with all laws; any warranty remedy beyond restore-or-terminate.
rules.hardLine: A warranty that the Product will be uninterrupted or error-free.
rules.source: CSA default; warranty remedy is exclusive; optional non-infringement warranty offered with 'U.S.' and 'patent' bracketed.

rules.title: Changes to the agreement
rules.guidance: Changes in writing, signed or accepted by both: the CSA default, which our standard terms keep. We welcome, but do not require, a right to update our operational policies (security, acceptable use, support) on notice, provided the update does not materially reduce the Customer's protections.
rules.preferred: Waivers and changes only in writing signed or accepted by each party (the CSA default). A right for us to update operational policies on notice without material reduction in the Customer's protections is welcome but not required.
rules.acceptable: Operational-policy updates on 30 days' notice with a right to object.
rules.escalation: A Customer right to bind us to its own policies 'as updated from time to time', or removal of an operational-policy update right that the agreement already gives us.
rules.source: CSA default: changes in writing by both; Standard Terms versions never change once posted. Our operational-policy carve-out diverges from the default and is stated as such; the customer playbook treats any 'as updated from time to time' incorporation as escalation, so the two sides conflict here by design. Amended 17 October 2026 (P8 clean-copy calibration, pass 1; tough-eval/v2/LAYER-A-FIXES.md): the preferred position required, and the escalation tier protected against the removal of, an operational-policy update right that our own standard terms do not contain, so the clean copy fell short of this playbook although its provenance says the clean copy deviates from nothing (flagged on p95 by Opus and DeepSeek). The right is now welcome but not required, and only removing it where the agreement gives it escalates.

rules.title: Assignment
rules.guidance: Either party may assign on notice after a merger, change of control or sale of substantially all relevant assets; otherwise consent. We must keep the change-of-control exception.
rules.preferred: Mutual consent requirement with the mutual merger and change-of-control exception on notice.
rules.acceptable: Consent not to be unreasonably withheld; assignment by either party to an affiliate on notice.
rules.escalation: Removal of the change-of-control exception for us, or a Customer right to assign to a competitor of ours.
rules.source: CSA default; alternatives offered via Other Changes (any affiliate, or prohibit entirely).

rules.title: Governing law and courts
rules.guidance: Our seat is England and Wales with the London courts. For large customers we accept their home law within the EU, England and Wales, or a US state with established commercial law.
rules.preferred: Governing Law: England and Wales. Chosen Courts: London, exclusive.
rules.acceptable: The law of an EU member state, Scotland, or Delaware, New York or California, with the corresponding courts.
rules.escalation: Any other law, or arbitration seated outside Europe or the United States.
rules.source: Key Terms leave governing law blank; 71% Delaware among signed CSAs. Our England and Wales seat follows the suite's Key Terms.

rules.title: Publicity
rules.guidance: We may name the Customer and use its logo to identify it as a customer. Customers often remove this; we accept removal.
rules.preferred: Name and logo use to identify the Customer as a customer.
rules.acceptable: No logo use, or use only with the Customer's prior approval.
rules.escalation: A prohibition on naming the Customer in required disclosures or to prospective investors under confidentiality.
rules.source: CSA default; 'some customers prefer to remove this grant'.

rules.title: Verification of use
rules.guidance: Our standard terms have no audit clause because the service meters usage. We ask for nothing more. We do not accept customer audits of our systems beyond our published security reports.
rules.preferred: No audit clause; usage measured by the service.
rules.acceptable: An annual self-certification of User numbers by the Customer; our provision of a current third-party security report on request.
rules.escalation: A Customer right to audit our systems or premises, or an obligation to permit penetration testing without agreement.
rules.source: The CSA has no audit clause. The customer playbook's 'no audit right' and our 'no audit clause' coincide, so a clean copy complies with both; the sides differ only on audits of the provider.

rules.title: Security incident notification
rules.guidance: We notify the Customer of a personal data breach without undue delay and within 72 hours of becoming aware, which lets the Customer meet its own deadline. We cannot promise a clock that starts before we know, nor notice of every attempted or unsuccessful attack.
rules.preferred: Notice without undue delay when feasible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware; timely information as it becomes known; prompt reasonable steps to contain and investigate; Security Incident means a Personal Data Breach under Article 4 of the GDPR.
rules.acceptable: Notice within 48 hours after becoming aware, or a written incident report within 30 days of notice.
rules.escalation: A notice deadline shorter than 48 hours after becoming aware, a deadline running from the incident rather than from our awareness, a Security Incident widened to suspected, attempted or unsuccessful incidents, or an obligation to notify data subjects or authorities on the Customer's behalf. Escalate to the Data Protection Officer.
rules.hardLine: Notice of attempted or unsuccessful incidents, or uncapped liability for incident costs.
rules.source: DPA Standard Terms section 4 (72 hours after becoming aware) and definition 11.15; Common Paper DPA v1.1 page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/data-processing-agreement/, read 15 October 2026): no annotation on notification timing, so the 72-hour default is our position; the 48-hour concession is ours.

rules.title: Subprocessors
rules.guidance: We run on a short list of approved subprocessors and must be able to change them with notice. The Customer gets written notice and a right to object, resolved in good faith; it cannot veto our infrastructure.
rules.preferred: Approved Subprocessors listed on the Cover Page; at least 10 business days' written notice of additions or replacements; 30 days to object, after which changes are deemed accepted; objections resolved in good faith.
rules.acceptable: Notice of up to 30 days, or a right for the Customer to terminate the affected service, without penalty and with a prorated refund, if an objection cannot be resolved.
rules.escalation: Notice longer than 30 days, prior specific written consent for each new subprocessor, a Customer veto, or a requirement to keep processing in a stated country. Escalate to the Data Protection Officer.
rules.hardLine: No subprocessor change without the Customer's consent at its discretion.
rules.source: DPA Standard Terms section 2.6(a); Common Paper DPA v1.1 page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/data-processing-agreement/, read 15 October 2026): "customers must receive at least 10 business days prior notice of any additions to or replacements on the list, even if the list is hosted online".

rules.title: Liability for subprocessors
rules.guidance: We stay responsible for our subprocessors as for ourselves, inside the liability terms of the Agreement; we do not take on a separate or uncapped liability for them.
rules.preferred: Provider remains fully liable for obligations subcontracted to its subprocessors, including their acts and omissions, and passes equivalent data protection terms down to them, within the limits of the Agreement; where the GDPR applies, Provider shares copies of its subprocessor agreements at the Customer's request, redacted to protect business secrets and other confidential information (DPA section 2.6(c) of our standard terms).
rules.acceptable: An added obligation to enforce the subprocessor agreement at the Customer's request.
rules.escalation: Liability for subprocessors outside the Agreement's caps or damages waiver, an indemnity for subprocessor acts, or a duty to give the Customer copies of subprocessor contracts beyond DPA section 2.6(c) (unredacted copies, or copies where the GDPR does not apply).
rules.source: DPA Standard Terms section 2.6(b) to (d) and section 8.1 (DPA liability subject to the Agreement); Common Paper DPA v1.1 page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/data-processing-agreement/, read 15 October 2026): no annotation on section 2.6(d). Amended 17 October 2026 (P8 clean-copy calibration, pass 1; tough-eval/v2/LAYER-A-FIXES.md): the escalation trigger 'a duty to give the Customer copies of subprocessor contracts' named a duty our own standard DPA contains (section 2.6(c): where the GDPR applies, at the Customer's request, with redaction), which contradicted this playbook's statement that the clean copy deviates from nothing (flagged on a26 by Opus and DeepSeek). The redacted GDPR copy duty is now part of the preferred position; anything beyond it still escalates.

rules.title: Audits and security reports
rules.guidance: Audit rights are exercised through our independent reports and an annual questionnaire, not by inspections of our systems. Routine compliance evidence is free; anything more is at the Customer's cost.
rules.preferred: Compliance information on request; audit rights exercised only through the Report and due-diligence questionnaires; questionnaires once a year, in writing to the Security Contact; records kept for 3 years; access restricted where it would harm our IP, confidentiality or legal obligations.
rules.acceptable: One on-site audit a year at the Customer's cost, on at least 30 days' notice, only where the Report and questionnaires do not answer a specific concern.
rules.escalation: Inspections on demand, audits more than once a year, audits at our cost, questionnaires more than once a year, records kept longer than 3 years, or removal of the restriction protecting our IP and confidentiality.
rules.hardLine: Unlimited on-site audits by the Customer or its auditors at our cost.
rules.source: DPA Standard Terms sections 5.1 to 5.3; Common Paper DPA v1.1 page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/data-processing-agreement/, read 15 October 2026): no annotation on section 5. The Common Paper CSA itself has no audit clause (common-paper-notes.md).

rules.title: Return and deletion of personal data
rules.guidance: When the DPA ends we return or delete personal data as the Customer instructs, keeping what the law requires and protecting it. We cannot purge rotating backups early or certify destruction of backup media.
rules.preferred: Return or deletion at the Customer's instruction after the DPA expires, except where storage is required or authorised by Applicable Law, with remaining data protected; deletion by the Customer through the Service as soon as reasonably practicable; a certificate of deletion only if asked for under the SCCs.
rules.acceptable: Deletion within 30 days after expiry, with a certificate of deletion on request.
rules.escalation: Deletion within fewer than 30 days, deletion of backups outside their normal rotation, certified destruction of backup media, or removal of the legal-retention exception.
rules.source: DPA Standard Terms section 7; Common Paper DPA v1.1 page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/data-processing-agreement/, read 15 October 2026): "there are many situations where you might be required to continue hosting or processing data".

rules.title: DPA liability and precedence
rules.guidance: Data protection claims sit inside the Agreement's liability structure (privacy and security breaches are Increased Claims under the increased cap). The SCCs prevail where the law requires; otherwise the order of precedence is fixed.
rules.preferred: Each party's liability under the DPA subject to the waivers, exclusions and limitations of the Agreement; claims only by the contracting Customer entity; order of precedence: the SCCs or UK Addendum, then the DPA, then the Agreement.
rules.acceptable: A separate DPA cap no higher than the Increased Cap Amount.
rules.escalation: DPA liability outside the Agreement's limits, a separate DPA cap above the Increased Cap Amount, claims by the Customer's affiliates, or the DPA made to prevail over the SCCs. Escalate to the General Counsel.
rules.hardLine: Uncapped liability under the DPA beyond what Applicable Data Protection Laws require.
rules.source: DPA Standard Terms sections 8 and 9; Common Paper DPA v1.1 page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/data-processing-agreement/, read 15 October 2026): a separate DPA Liability Cap field "will override those values and set a separate dollar amount"; related-party claims clause "makes it so that Customer's affiliates ... are barred from bringing claims".

rules.title: Service levels and credits
rules.guidance: Our SLA is 99.9% monthly uptime and a 4 business hour response, with credits that apply to future fees only and are capped. Credits enforce the SLA without being punitive.
rules.preferred: Target Uptime 99.9% per month, measured as the SLA defines; Uptime Credits of 5%, 10% and 25% of the monthly fee by band; Target Response Time 4 business hours with a 2% Response Time Credit; credits only against future fees, never cash; claims within 7 days of month end; credits capped at 8% of the Subscription Period's fees.
rules.acceptable: A credit cap of up to 10% of the Subscription Period's fees, a claim window of up to 30 days, or a Target Response Time of 2 business hours.
rules.escalation: Target Uptime above 99.9%, credits above the bands, a cap above 10%, credits payable in cash or as refunds, a claim window longer than 30 days, Scheduled Downtime or Excluded Minutes counted as downtime, or a response target under 2 business hours. Escalate to the Commercial Director.
rules.source: SLA Standard Terms sections 1 to 3; Common Paper SLA v2.0 page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/service-level-agreement/, read 15 October 2026): credits "only apply towards future invoices" so the SLA is "enforceable but not overly punitive"; the 8% cap is "an overall maximum for accrued service credits"; target uptime examples run from 99.999% (customer-favourable) to 98% (vendor-favourable); SLAs appear in 39% of CSAs (2024 Q1 benchmark).

rules.title: Service level remedies
rules.guidance: Credits are the exclusive remedy for missing the uptime and response targets. Chronic failure lets the Customer leave with a refund, but only after we have had notice and a chance to fix it.
rules.preferred: Service credits the exclusive remedy and our entire liability for missing the Target Uptime and Target Response Time; termination of the affected Order Form, with a prorated refund, after the Target Uptime is missed in 2 out of any 3 consecutive months, each failure notified within 7 days of month end.
rules.acceptable: Termination after failures in 3 of any 6 months, on the same notice condition.
rules.escalation: Termination after a single month's failure, termination without the notice condition, removal of the exclusive-remedy clause, or credits or termination extended to failures other than uptime and response time.
rules.hardLine: Damages for SLA failures in addition to credits.
rules.source: SLA Standard Terms sections 3.4 and 3.5; Common Paper SLA v2.0 page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/service-level-agreement/, read 15 October 2026): "It is very common for SLAs to provide the exclusive remedy for issues subject to the SLA"; termination "In the event of serious issues that occur in 2 out of 3 consecutive months", the notice requirement giving vendors a chance to fix problems.
